summary.headline: Your reporting mixes three attribution models, never closes the loop on revenue, and has no fast alert — you would not catch AI output tanking conversion until the quarter closed.
summary.narrative: Across 8 campaign rows the attribution model switches between First-touch, Last-touch, and Multi-touch, so revenue is not comparable row to row. There is no cadence tying won revenue back to originating content fast enough to act, and no leading-indicator alerting on bounce, unsubscribe, or conversion drops. Standardize attribution, close the loop weekly, and add a circuit-breaker alert before enabling any AI content step.

findings.title: Three attribution models mixed in one report
findings.what_we_found: The reporting credits revenue using First-touch (Webinar Q1, Content Syndication), Last-touch (Paid Search, Newsletter, Paid Social, Referral Program), and Multi-touch (Tradeshow) on different rows of the same export.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: Numbers are not comparable row to row, so an AI optimizing spend or content against them would chase artifacts of the model rather than real performance.
the_fix: Pick one primary attribution model and apply it consistently across all campaigns.
If multiple models are needed, report them in parallel columns, never mixed per-row.
Re-baseline historical rows to the chosen model before any AI optimizes against the data.
findings.evidence: attribution_model column contains 'First-touch', 'Last-touch', and 'Multi-touch' across the 8 rows.

findings.title: No closed feedback loop on conversion and revenue
findings.what_we_found: Reporting shows leads through won/revenue by campaign-month, but there is no evidence won revenue is tied back to the originating content on a cadence fast enough to act — two channels (Content Syndication, Paid Social) show 0 won with no follow-up signal.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: Without a closed loop, an AI's content output cannot be evaluated and corrected; underperforming output would keep running and the failure would compound silently.
the_fix: Tie won revenue back to the originating campaign/content on a weekly or faster cadence.
Define a per-content conversion baseline so deviations are detectable.
Review the loop with a named owner before any AI content step goes live.
findings.evidence: Monthly rollup only; 0-won rows with no downstream tie-back.

findings.title: No leading-indicator alerting
findings.what_we_found: Reporting is monthly and lagging; there is no leading-indicator alerting on bounce/unsubscribe spikes, conversion-rate drops, or deliverability dips that would fire within hours.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: A leading-indicator alert is the circuit-breaker that lets a human pause an AI content step before damage goes broad. Without it, an AI could degrade conversion or deliverability for weeks before anyone notices.
the_fix: Instrument leading indicators: bounce rate, unsubscribe rate, reply/spam complaints, conversion-rate delta, deliverability score.
Set thresholds that fire within hours to a named human owner.
Document a pause/rollback action tied to the alert as the AI-step circuit-breaker.
findings.evidence: No alerting or leading-indicator columns present in the reporting export.
